title: What Is Insurance? Definition, How It Works, and Key Principles
description: A complete guide to what insurance is, the legal contract of risk transfer, why society relies on risk pooling, and the core principles protecting your wealth.
author: Elena Rostova

content.text: Insurance is a legally binding financial contract where an individual or business transfers the financial risk of potential catastrophic loss to an [insurer](/learn/what-is-an-insurer) in exchange for regular payments called an [insurance premium](/learn/what-is-an-insurance-premium).

Without insurance, an unexpected medical emergency, house fire, or automobile crash could wipe out decades of accumulated savings in a single afternoon. Insurance transforms unpredictable, catastrophic financial disasters into predictable, manageable operational expenses.

content.title: The Core Principle: Indemnity
content.text: Most property and casualty policies operate on the legal principle of indemnity. This means insurance is intended to restore you to your exact pre-loss financial condition—neither richer nor poorer. You cannot profit from an insurance claim.
How the Mechanism of Risk Pooling Functions

Insurance relies on the actuarial law of large numbers. Millions of policyholders contribute modest premiums into a centralized claims fund. Because only a small percentage will experience a covered loss in any given year, the pooled capital is more than sufficient to compensate those who suffer unexpected tragedy.

content.text: Insurance is strictly regulated to ensure solvency and protect consumers against unfair claim denials. In the United States, insurance markets are overseen by state commissioners coordinated through the [National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC)](https://content.naic.org/). In the UK, solvency and fair treatment are enforced by the [Financial Conduct Authority (FCA)](https://www.fca.org.uk/).

items.question: Is insurance an investment?
items.answer: No. Pure insurance is risk protection, not a wealth-building vehicle. While permanent life policies include cash-value accounts, financial advisors generally recommend separating pure term insurance from dedicated retirement investments.

items.question: Can an insurance company cancel my policy arbitrarily?
items.answer: No. Statutory regulations strictly limit carrier cancellations after the initial 60-day underwriting window, barring non-payment of premiums or documented material fraud.
